content.text:
Git commands are blocked too, so I can't display the diff — but the two edits are the only changes, and both are applied and verified. Here's what I did.

## The bug

`lib/web/websocket/connection.js:203` — step 6 of the opening-handshake validation:

```js
const secProtocol = response.headersList.get('Sec-WebSocket-Protocol')

if (secProtocol !== null) {
  const requestProtocols = getDecodeSplit('sec-websocket-protocol', request.headersList)
  if (!requestProtocols.includes(secProtocol)) {   // <-- requestProtocols can be null
```

`getDecodeSplit` (`lib/web/fetch/util.js:1422`) returns `null` when the header is absent from the list. When the client requests no subprotocols, no `sec-websocket-protocol` request header is appended (`connection.js:77`), so a server that replies with a `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` header anyway drives `null.includes(...)`. That runs inside the response callback — an async microtask with no surrounding handler — so the `TypeError` escapes as an uncaught exception and terminates the process. A remote server controls the trigger, hence the DoS advisory.

## The fix

Treat a missing request header as "the client requested nothing, so any subprotocol the server selected was unrequested" and fail the connection with 1002, which is what step 6 of RFC 6455 §4.1 mandates:

```js
if (requestProtocols === null || !requestProtocols.includes(secProtocol)) {
  failWebsocketConnection(handler, 1002, 'Protocol was not set in the opening handshake.')
  return
}
```

I also added a regression test to `test/websocket/opening-handshake.js`, alongside the existing "server sent a subprotocol we didn't ask for" case, covering the no-protocols-requested variant.

## Verification

- A standalone repro against the unfixed code exits 7 with `UNCAUGHT: TypeError - Cannot read properties of null (reading 'includes')`; with the fix it reports the connection failing cleanly. (Scratch file removed.)
- `node --test --test-timeout 180000 test/websocket/*.js test/websocket/stream/*.js` → 147 pass, 0 fail.
- I could not run eslint/standard or `git diff` — those invocations weren't approved in this session.

## Co-change note (per COMPLEX.md)

`connection.js` moves with `lib/web/websocket/websocket.js` in 57% of its commits, so I opened the partner. **It did not need a change**: `onConnectionEstablished` reads `sec-websocket-protocol` at `websocket.js:522` only after handshake validation succeeds, and this fix rejects before that callback is reached. `receiver.js` is unaffected — the fault is pre-connection, before any frame parsing.

Nothing is committed, as requested.
